Read by day_track.graduate() at the Monday calibration.

exit.SUPERSEDES_THE_14_00Z_RATCHET_AND_WHY: The concurrent 13:45Z run's management pass (preserved in full in this row's 'management' array, and NOT deleted) ratcheted the stop 707.86 -> 708.95 at +2.44R and left status 'open'. rows._manage_note_2026-09-21: BREAKEVEN ARMED 13 MINUTES AFTER THE PAPER ENTRY. Unrealized +$2.06 on the single share (+1.43R at the bid); worst excursion since entry was -0.28R. THE ENTRY WINDOW WAS NARROWER THAN THE RUN CADENCE, AND THAT IS THE ONE THING THIS DAY TEACHES: the 13:37Z sibling cleared the late-entry gate with 0.09 of a point to spare (729.2575 against a 729.35 ceiling = OR high 728.84 + 0.5 x the 1.02-point range), and by 13:45Z plan_entry() on the same OR returns action='skip', reason='late entry', because QQQ was 731.28 — 2.44 points beyond the edge on a 1.02-point range. Both calls are correct. The spec allows entry across 09:35-09:50 ET, but a 1.02-point opening range on a tape running +1.2% keeps that window open for roughly EIGHT minutes, not fifteen. Nothing here needs changing: the gate refused to chase and the sibling that fired inside the window took the signal cleanly. It is logged because it bears on go-live scheduling, not because either decision was wrong. *** 14:05Z UPDATE: the 2R trail ARMED and the stop ratcheted 729.2575 -> 730.8469 (+1.106R locked). QQQ bid 732.58, +2.31R, peak 732.67. Also note the sign flip against the 09-16 finding: there the stale prior-session bars DRAGGED ATR DOWN (placid close) and tightened the trail; today they RAISE it (today-only gap-free ATR5 is 1.05 against the as-spec 1.2154), loosening it. The contamination's DIRECTION is not stable, which the 09-16 write-up did not claim but a reader could easily infer from its single observation. *** 14:33Z UPDATE: THIRD RATCHET, 731.5264 -> 733.0714, locking +2.653R with the position at +4.11R (QQQ 735.17, +$5.91 on the single share). This is now comfortably the best trade the paper track has produced -- the prior three paper days were -1R each. Two things worth carrying forward and neither is a rule change: (1) the trail is doing exactly the job it was designed for on the only trending day the track has seen, converting an unrealized run into a locked floor that ratchets with the tape rather than a fixed target that would have capped it; (2) the 1-share quantization the entry row flagged cuts BOTH ways -- +4.11R reads as a headline but is $5.91 of actual money, and a track that can only express conviction in whole $735 units will keep producing R-multiples that overstate the dollars. Judge the graduation on R, size the live track on dollars, and do not let the two be confused in the weekly review.
